name: Carrot
notes__en:
The Carrot is the crop most players plant first, and it is the default crop in our calculator for that reason. It is a Common crop that is harvested once: when you pick it, the plant is gone and you need a new seed.

Its base value is small, so a plain Carrot is never going to carry your garden. What makes it useful is that it is a cheap way to learn how the price formula works. A Carrot heavier than its listed base weight sells for more, because the wiki formula squares the weight ratio, while a lighter one never drops much below the base price.

If a Carrot rolls a Gold or Rainbow variant, or picks up a strong mutation such as Shocked, the multipliers apply to the same small base. That is why a mutated Carrot is a nice surprise but still worth far less than the same mutation on a higher-value crop.

name: Strawberry
notes__en:
Strawberry is a Common crop, but unlike the Carrot it keeps producing fruit after the first harvest. That multi-harvest behaviour is the main reason to plant it early: one seed keeps paying out instead of being used up.

Each single Strawberry is worth very little, even less than a Carrot at base. The value comes from volume over time, so it suits players who check their garden often. Because every fruit is a fresh roll, a Strawberry plant also gives you many chances at a heavy fruit or a mutation from one seed.

Use the weight table on this page to see how much a bigger berry adds. A fruit at double the base weight is worth roughly four times as much, since the formula squares the weight ratio.

name: Blueberry
notes__en:
Blueberry is an Uncommon crop that regrows after harvest, so one plant keeps giving fruit. It has the lightest base weight of the early berries we track, which matters when you read the weight table: even a small gain in grams is a large gain in percentage terms.

Its base value is level with the Carrot, so on its own it is a starter crop. Treat a Blueberry bush as a steady trickle rather than a money maker, and as a cheap test bed for mutations: every new berry is another roll.

When you sell, look at the weight before anything else. The formula only rewards weight above the base value listed here, and a berry under that weight is rounded up to almost full price, so tiny berries are not a loss.

name: Corn
notes__en:
Corn is a Rare crop and it regrows after harvest. Its base value is the highest of the early crops on this list, and its base weight is noticeably heavier than the berries, so a plain ear of Corn already sells for more than a plain Tomato.

Because it keeps producing, Corn is a good crop to leave growing while you work on other things. Every ear is a separate roll for weight, variant and mutations.

Our tip: when an ear of Corn shows a strong mutation, check it in the calculator before selling. Mutation bonuses add together in the wiki formula, so two or three mutations on one ear stack up quickly even on a mid-value crop.

name: Tomato
notes__en:
Tomato is a Rare crop that produces again after you harvest it. Its base value sits a little above the Carrot and Blueberry but well below the Legendary crops, so it is a middle step while you save up for better seeds.

The good part is that it stays planted. A garden full of multi-harvest crops like Tomato keeps making fruit while you are away, and every fruit can roll its own variant and mutations.

We would not keep Tomatoes forever. Once you can afford crops with a much larger base value, the same mutations are worth far more there. Until then, they are a solid filler for empty plots.

name: Apple
notes__en:
Apple is a Legendary crop that regrows, which makes it unusual: many Legendary crops are single harvest, but an Apple tree keeps dropping fruit. Each Apple has a modest base value for its rarity, much lower than Bamboo or Pumpkin, and it has a higher huge chance than most crops we track.

That mix makes the Apple a crop you plant for the long run. You give up some value per fruit, but you get many fruits from one seed, and each one is another chance at a big or mutated Apple.

If you only have room for a few plots, compare it with Bamboo using the calculator. Bamboo gives more per harvest, while the Apple tree keeps giving without replanting.

name: Bamboo
notes__en:
Bamboo is a Legendary crop with the highest base value of the Legendary crops covered in this first batch of notes (Apple, Pumpkin and Watermelon are the others), and it has the highest huge chance of the crops we have written notes for. The catch is that it is a single-harvest crop: once you cut it, you need another seed.

That makes Bamboo a crop for players who actively replant. Each stalk is worth a lot at base, so variants and mutations on Bamboo turn into large numbers fast.

Weight still matters. Bamboo has a heavy base weight, so read the weight table on this page instead of guessing. A stalk below the base weight is only lightly reduced, but one well above it can be worth several times the base price.

name: Pumpkin
notes__en:
Pumpkin is a Legendary crop and it is harvested once. Its base weight is heavy, and its base value is a bit higher than the Watermelon, the other big single-harvest Legendary.

Because a Pumpkin is used up on harvest, you get one roll per seed. That makes the variant on each Pumpkin important: a Gold or Rainbow Pumpkin is a big jump over a plain one, as the variant table above shows.

Big Pumpkins are where the weight formula really shows. The price grows with the square of how heavy it is compared with its base weight, so an oversized Pumpkin can be worth far more than the listed base.

name: Watermelon
notes__en:
Watermelon is a Legendary single-harvest crop with a heavy base weight. Its base value is close to Pumpkin's but a little lower, so the two are a fair comparison when you choose what to plant.

Like Pumpkin, a Watermelon gives one roll per seed. That makes it a crop for players who replant often and who want each harvest to be worth something on its own.

When a Watermelon comes out large, check the weight table: the price grows with the square of the weight ratio. Mutations then add on top, and several mutations add their bonuses together rather than multiplying each other.

name: Coconut
notes__en:
Coconut is a Mythical crop that regrows, but its numbers surprise people. It has one of the heaviest base weights on our list, yet its base value is much lower than other Mythical crops such as Cactus or Dragon Fruit.

That means a Coconut is about steady output, not big single sales. The palm keeps producing, and every coconut is a fresh chance at a variant or mutation.

Because the base weight is so large, a coconut that looks heavy may still be close to average. Compare its weight with the base weight on this page before you expect a big price, or simply enter it into the calculator.
